cohort: The study included 150 full-term, first-time mothers admitted for labor induction, randomly assigned to receive either misoprostol or cerviprime gel.
finding: Misoprostol significantly reduced the time to onset of labor, induction-to-delivery interval, need for oxytocin augmentation, and induction cost compared to cerviprime gel, while maintaining comparable maternal and neonatal safety profiles.
mod_finding: The misoprostol group experienced a 2% higher rate of cesarean sections compared to the cerviprime group.
